defects.class: negative length recorded as size_t -> out-of-bounds read
defects.description: pkey_dh_ctrl's EVP_PKEY_CTRL_DH_KDF_UKM arm stored p1 directly in kdf_ukmlen (a size_t). A C-valid negative p1 with a non-NULL p2 became a huge length, and a later X9.42 derive passed it to DH_KDF_X9_42, which reads that many UKM bytes. The authority stores the same value and has the same defect; no safe Rust caller reaches the arm because the current candidate has no legacy pmeth dispatch, but the exported method table makes it latent.
defects.fix: The arm refuses a non-NULL p2 paired with p1 < 0 with -2, before releasing or replacing the stored block. Every non-negative length preserves the authority's behaviour exactly; NULL p2 still clears the length to 0.
defects.witness: dh::pmeth::tests::a_negative_ukm_length_is_refused installs the method context with pkey_dh_init, calls the ctrl with p1 = -1, asserts -2, then runs the method's own cleanup.

defects.class: unchecked allocation-offset arithmetic -> heap out-of-bounds write
defects.description: TXT_DB_read computed add = (num + 1) * sizeof(char *) in c_int and later allocated add + offset bytes, using add as the row's data cursor. A large C-valid num makes the product wrap (in debug it panics inside guard_ffi; in release it can wrap to 0 or negative). The index and qualifier array allocations precede it, so under Linux overcommit a caller passing num = 2^29 - 1 can reach the parse with both arrays allocated; add then wraps to 0, the row is sized only by the line length, and the field/sentinel pointer stores write past it.
defects.fix: Both products/sums are now computed with checked_add/checked_mul and usize::try_from; any overflow takes the existing read_err path (which releases buf, data, index, qual and the object at the authority's error coordinates). Valid num values take the same allocation sizes, order and return values as before.
defects.witness: No in-module test exists and the control would require multi-gigabyte virtual allocations, so this is recorded as a BOUNDARY NOT_RUN rather than claimed as tested. The change is arithmetic with a total failure arm; the full library suite exercises the valid path through srp::srp_vfy's TXT_DB_read. The post-fix srp tests pass.
